key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while blue-shifting its band gap.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial design of perovskite solar absorbers where static calculations miss dynamic structural and optical responses.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track structural changes and average band gaps over MD snapshots.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with experiments on MAPbI₃ films on KCl, bulk and slab trends are consistent, and ensemble band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift.
watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate interfaces, so interface-specific effects remain an implementation concern.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
